concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
question: After the indigo revolution in Bengal, where did the planters shift their operations?
solution: The correct answer is __**Bihar**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • After the **Indigo Revolution** in Bengal, many planters faced resistance from farmers due to the oppressive conditions of cultivation under the **Indigo system**. • The movement against indigo farming in Bengal was led by farmers who refused to grow indigo, culminating in the famous **Indigo Revolt of 1859-60**. • As a result of the revolt, the planters shifted their operations to **Bihar**, where they continued indigo cultivation under more favorable conditions. • Bihar became a significant center for indigo production in colonial India, as the soil and climatic conditions were suitable for indigo cultivation. • Historical records highlight that indigo cultivation in Bihar persisted until synthetic dyes began to replace natural indigo in the early 20th century.
